Shadow AI discovery is the part of AI governance that IT teams inherit without being asked. Nobody sends a memo announcing that the sales team pasted a customer contract into a chat tool, that an engineer connected a coding assistant to the production repository, or that finance trials four summarisation tools on last quarter's board pack. title: Is It Safe to Delete ~/Library/Caches on a Mac? How to Clear Cache Safely
summary:
Yes—most subfolders inside ~/Library/Caches are safe to delete on a Mac, as long as you quit running apps first, remove only the contents inside (never the Caches folder itself), and skip Apple system caches and sensitive tool data. Apps automatically recreate their cache files the next time you open them, so the only normal side effect is a slightly slower first launch or re-downloading cached assets.

What you should not touch are macOS's system-wide /Library/Caches and /System/Library/Caches folders—macOS manages those itself. Also keep expectations realistic: clearing cache reclaims disk space, not RAM or CPU performance; in fact, rebuilding caches can briefly use a little extra disk and network activity right after cleanup.

title: How we keep a Laravel log ingest endpoint fast (Valkey buffer, batched ClickHouse writes)
summary:
We're building a hosted log tool on Laravel 13, and the part that took the most thought was ingestion. Clients send logs in bursts, sometimes thousands of lines a second, and the endpoint can't sit waiting on a database while that happens.

The request does almost nothing

It checks the token, pushes the batch into Valkey (Redis-compatible) and returns a 202. There are no MySQL queries in that path and no queue job per line.

Drainers do the writing

Separate long-running drainer processes, one per buffer shard, claim a batch of 500 to 1000 lines, insert it into ClickHouse, and only acknowledge it after the insert succeeded. Popping first and writing second looks simpler, but it loses lines if the process dies in between.
